newsitem.title: USA: US Commerce's Ehrlich says data understate growth.
newsitem.headline: US Commerce's Ehrlich says data understate growth.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich said on Friday that government statistics were most likely understating growth and overstating inflation.
"We must always be aware of the problems of measurement," Ehrlich told an Atlantic Economic Society conference.

Ehrlich said the measurement problems stemmed from the difficulty of measuring more intangible products such as those generated in the software and pharmaceuticals industries, rather than primarily tallying up the types of goods that can be purchased in a supermarket or other stores.
Ehrlich was upbeat overall about U.S. economic prospects, citing the progress brought about by new technology.
"The U.S. economy looks to have very strong growth prospects in the years and days ahead," he said.
